title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Robert Jay Josett, 35, a former Costa Mesa officer, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors, including unauthorized computer access and fraud, repeated phone calls, and violating a restraining order. Over nine months, he contacted his mistress thousands of times by text, phone, and social media, sometimes more than 100 times a day. After she ended the relationship in April 2024, he threatened to reveal explicit photos, called her and her new boyfriend as many as 58 times in a day, and drove by her home.

Between June and December 2023, Josett made 13 non-job-related inquiries in the CLETS law enforcement database about his mistress and his wife. He also used the FLOCK license plate reader system to track her vehicle, and in June 2024, after being placed on leave, he used it to find her new boyfriend's address. He was served with a protective order on June 28, 2024, then violated the order by driving by her home and was arrested. He received three years informal probation and must complete a 52-week domestic violence program. His POST certification review is pending.
